final_proof:
Write \(f(t)=u(t)+iv(t)\), where \(u=\operatorname{Re}(f)\) and \(v=\operatorname{Im}(f)\). Since \(f\) is continuous, \(u\) and \(v\) are continuous real-valued functions on \([a,b]\). We first prove the required additivity for an arbitrary continuous real-valued function \(g\) on \([a,b]\).

If \(c=a\) or \(c=b\), the result follows immediately from the convention that the integral over a degenerate interval is zero. Now suppose \(a<c<b\), and put
\[
A=\int_a^c g(t)\,dt+\int_c^b g(t)\,dt.
\]
Both integrals exist because \(g\) is continuous. We show directly from the tagged-partition characterization of the Riemann integral that \(A\) is the integral of \(g\) over \([a,b]\).

Let \(\varepsilon>0\). There are positive numbers \(\delta_L\) and \(\delta_R\) such that every tagged Riemann sum for \(g\) on \([a,c]\) having mesh less than \(\delta_L\) differs from \(\int_a^c g(t)\,dt\) by less than \(\varepsilon/4\), and every tagged Riemann sum on \([c,b]\) having mesh less than \(\delta_R\) differs from \(\int_c^b g(t)\,dt\) by less than \(\varepsilon/4\). Moreover, uniform continuity of \(g\) on the compact interval \([a,b]\) gives \(\delta_0>0\) such that
\[
|g(x)-g(y)|<\frac{\varepsilon}{2(b-a)}
\]
whenever \(x,y\in[a,b]\) and \(|x-y|<\delta_0\). Set
\[
\delta=\min\{\delta_L,\delta_R,\delta_0\},
\]
and consider any tagged partition \(P\) of \([a,b]\) whose mesh is less than \(\delta\).

If \(c\) is a partition point of \(P\), splitting \(P\) at \(c\) produces tagged partitions \(P_L\) of \([a,c]\) and \(P_R\) of \([c,b]\), and
\[
|S(P,g)-A|
\leq \left|S(P_L,g)-\int_a^c g\right|
 +\left|S(P_R,g)-\int_c^b g\right|
<\frac{\varepsilon}{2}.
\]

If \(c\) is not a partition point, there is a unique subinterval \([x_{k-1},x_k]\) of \(P\) containing \(c\) in its interior. Split this subinterval at \(c\). Keep all the original tags outside this subinterval, and choose arbitrary valid tags \(\eta_L\in[x_{k-1},c]\) and \(\eta_R\in[c,x_k]\) for its two pieces. This gives tagged partitions \(P_L\) and \(P_R\) of \([a,c]\) and \([c,b]\), both with mesh less than \(\delta\). If \(\xi\) is the original tag in \([x_{k-1},x_k]\), then the difference between the original sum and the sum of the two new sums is confined to this subinterval and is at most
\[
|g(\xi)-g(\eta_L)|(c-x_{k-1})
+|g(\xi)-g(\eta_R)|(x_k-c)
<\frac{\varepsilon}{2(b-a)}(x_k-x_{k-1})
\leq \frac{\varepsilon}{2}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
|S(P,g)-A|<\frac{\varepsilon}{2}+ rac{\varepsilon}{4}+ rac{\varepsilon}{4}=\varepsilon.
\]
Thus every sufficiently fine tagged Riemann sum on \([a,b]\) is arbitrarily close to \(A\). Hence
\[
\int_a^b g(t)\,dt
=\int_a^c g(t)\,dt+\int_c^b g(t)\,dt.
\]

Apply this real-valued result first to \(u\) and then to \(v\). By the componentwise definition of the integral of a complex-valued function,
\[
\int_p^q f(t)\,dt
=\int_p^q u(t)\,dt+i\int_p^q v(t)\,dt
\]
for every subinterval \([p,q]\subseteq[a,b]\). Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_a^c f(t)\,dt+\int_c^b f(t)\,dt
&=\left(\int_a^c u+\int_c^b u\right)
+i\left(\int_a^c v+\int_c^b v\right)\\
&=\int_a^b u+i\int_a^b v\\
&=\int_a^b f(t)\,dt.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the desired identity.
